extracted.intended_audience: talented early-career researchers preparing an ERC Starting Grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Starting Grant proposal (eligibility, host institution, application contents, funding rules, evaluation and ethics review). Targeted at early-career researchers (2–7 years since PhD) seeking independent ERC funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (experience window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 2023 the certified date of the successful PhD defence is used as the reference point for calculating the eligibility window (see separate entry). Applicants should check the ERC Work Programme for details. Eligibility can be extended for certain reasons (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility can be extended for reasons such as maternity, paternity, or parental leave, illness, national service, clinical training, natural disasters, asylum, or for victims of gender-based violence or any other form of violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Parental leave webpage and the latest ERC Work Programme to find the specific rules regarding eligibility criteria and how to claim extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD defence date reference
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2023, the European Research Council (ERC) changed the reference date for calculating the eligibility window: instead of the date of the actual award, the certified date of the successful PhD defence will be used as a reference point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aims to ensure fair competition across countries where the term 'award' varies. For applicants where no defence/viva was organised in the awarding institution, provide a written confirmation from that institution stating that no defence/viva was organised and indicating the date when the PhD was approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field eligibility — bottom-up approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research. The ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC has annual calls covering all scientific fields. Choose the call appropriate for your project and panel domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (known as a host institution/HI) located in one of the EU Member States or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host institution could be the HI where the applicant already works or any other HI in an EU Member State or associated country. The host must offer suitable conditions for the PI to independently lead the research and manage funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator (PI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant require a single Principal Investigator (PI) to submit the application on behalf of their host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI must be able to independently lead the research and manage funds. The PI does not need to be employed by the host institution at the time of proposal submission, but a mutual agreement and commitment are necessary if the proposal is successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and staffing flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members; it is also possible to have one or more team members located in a non-European country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies for team members can be published on the Euraxess-Jobs portal. Initiatives ('Implementing Arrangements') exist for ERC-funded teams in Europe to host non-European talented scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and additional funding eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for shorter durations). An additional €1 million can be made available to cover further eligible costs when necessary; for PIs currently based in non-associated third countries relocating to the EU/associated country, the maximum additional funding may be up to €2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional funding must be duly justified in the proposal. Consider major equipment, access to large facilities, start-up costs, major experimental and field work costs as potential reasons for additional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible costs coverage (direct and indirect)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget your proposal accordingly and ensure cost items meet eligibility rules in the call documents and Work Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals; calls are published on the ERC page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal of the EU. Familiarise yourself with the call documents and the 'EU submission service' online submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing, versioning and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your proposal as early as possible. Deadlines cannot be changed under any circumstances. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version, which will overwrite the old one. You will get an 'acknowledgement of receipt' by e-mail for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for host institution coordination and external review of drafts. Contact your National Contact Point (NCP) for support and start submission early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. Excellence is applied to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the proposal to demonstrate both the scientific excellence of the project and the PI's potential to lead it. See Guide for peer reviewers for details on how 'excellence' is interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process: peer review, quality threshold, ranking and budgetary cut-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess and score proposals. Those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand scoring and ranking implications: achieving the quality threshold is necessary but not sufficient; high ranking relative to other proposals is required given budget limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panels and expert roles
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 28 panels covering sub-sections of three domains (Life Sciences (LS), Physical and Engineering Sciences (PE), Social Sciences and Humanities (SH)). Each ERC panel consists of a chair and 10-16 members selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of scientific reputation. Panel members act as 'generalists' and evaluations rely on input from remote referees (specialised expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the deadline panel chairs are published on the ERC website; panel members are published after the evaluation process. Use panel information to judge which panel/domain best fits your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement and basis in application
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal is selected for funding it will undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed Ethics Self-Assessment (ESA) is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages, follow-up and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre-screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff) to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues; Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers) to identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues; Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers) to discuss Serious and/or Complex ethics issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearance of proposals with non-Serious and/or Complex ethics issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file and provided to ERCEA upon request. After screening applicants might be contacted (typically one week after the screening panel) and are given 3 weeks to reply. If follow-up is needed during project implementation, ethics deliverables might be formulated. Research proposals involving the use of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) will need to undergo all ethics steps and a specific EC approval following consultation to the HE programme committee (comitology) as required by law.
